pr_title: crosscluster/logical: handle user-defined types in SQL mode
pr_body:
This PR also includes a cleanup refactor:

### importer,crosscluster: move type resolver to a different package

Since we're using this type resolver for more than just IMPORT, it makes
more sense to put it in a more fitting package.

----

### crosscluster/logical: handle user-defined types in SQL mode

Previously, using a user-defined type in SQL mode would fail because of
a low level check in the execution engine that verifies that the input
datum has the same type OID as the destination column.

This does not work for LDR, since the input datums come directly from a
source table in a different cluster, so user-defined types have
different OIDs.

This fixes it by setting the datum type to "unknown" before executing
the insert query. The "unknown" type is what is normally used when any
SQL statement is sent to CRDB without explicit type annotations/hints.
When the execution engine sees this type, it will perform an automatic
(and cheap) immutable assignment cast to change the datum to the
appropriate type.

fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/132164
Release note (ops change): Logical replication streams that reference
tables with user-defined types can now be created with the `mode =
immediate` option.

issue_context.title: eval: create TypeResolver that can hydrate a Table with foreign type descriptors
issue_context.body:
When https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/131130 merges, LDR will use Import's type resolver to hydrate the source table descriptors with the source side type descriptors [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/849d013c758c4b76cdd9c9e0372e71eab00acabe/pkg/ccl/crosscluster/logical/logical_replication_job.go#L363). While this works for the kv path in LDR, the sql ingestion path panics with the following message:
```
panic: invalid datum type given: USER DEFINED ENUM: my_enum, expected USER DEFINED ENUM: public.my_enum
```
This panic occurs because the source type and dest type OID's mismatch:
https://github.com/msbutler/cockroach/blob/butler-udt-check/pkg/sql/types/types.go#L2163

This oid's are compared because the sql path passes datums to the sql statement [here](https://github.com/msbutler/cockroach/blob/butler-udt-check/pkg/ccl/crosscluster/logical/lww_row_processor.go#L515)

To avoid this panic, we need to build a new kind of the type resolver which allows us to hydrate the source table descriptor with the source types, but that prevents this sort of panic. Perhaps this type resolver _also_ requires the dest type descriptors as input? I'm unsure.


Jira issue: CRDB-42859

Epic CRDB-41465
comments: I also wonder if this new resolver could help us support source and dest enum's that are logically equivalent but not physically equivalent. For example, if the source enum is `color: blue=1, green =2` and the dest enum is `color: green=1, blue =2`. But maybe this translation needs to occur outside of the foundations logic.

Hi @benbardin, please add branch-* labels to identify which branch(es) this GA-blocker affects.
